def transform(grid):
    # Draw an axis-aligned diagonal connecting the two distinct marker cells.
    pts = [(r,c,v) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    if len(pts) >= 2:
        r1,c1,v1 = pts[0]
        r2,c2,v2 = pts[1]
        dr = 1 if r2 > r1 else -1 if r2 < r1 else 0
        dc = 1 if c2 > c1 else -1 if c2 < c1 else 0
        if abs(r2-r1) == abs(c2-c1):
            for k in range(1, abs(r2-r1)):
                out[r1+dr*k][c1+dc*k] = v1
    return out

def transform(grid):
    pts = [(r, c, v) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    if len(pts) == 2:
        (r1, c1, v1), (r2, c2, v2) = pts
        dr, dc = r2-r1, c2-c1
        # Fill the row-major sequence between the two differently colored markers.
        # With non-diagonal offsets, extend as a straight segment using integer steps
        # only when both coordinate distances divide into equal-sized steps.
        import math
        n = math.gcd(abs(dr), abs(dc))
        if n:
            sr, sc = dr//n, dc//n
            for k in range(1, n):
                out[r1+sr*k][c1+sc*k] = v1
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    ones = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v == 1]
    twos = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v == 2]
    if not ones or not twos:
        return out
    r, c = ones[0]
    tr, tc = twos[0]
    sr = 1 if tr > r else -1 if tr < r else 0
    sc = 1 if tc > c else -1 if tc < c else 0
    # Continue diagonally until reaching the target's row or column, then
    # finish straight toward the marker while stopping one cell short.
    while abs(tr-r) > 1 and abs(tc-c) > 1:
        r += sr
        c += sc
        out[r][c] = 3
    if abs(tr-r) <= 1:
        while c + sc != tc:
            c += sc
            out[r][c] = 3
    else:
        while r + sr != tr:
            r += sr
            out[r][c] = 3
    return out

def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    ones = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v == 1]
    twos = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, v in enumerate(row) if v == 2]
    if not ones or not twos:
        return out
    r, c = ones[0]
    tr, tc = twos[0]
    sr = 1 if tr > r else -1 if tr < r else 0
    sc = 1 if tc > c else -1 if tc < c else 0
    # Follow diagonal while both offsets exceed one; then continue straight
    # along the remaining offset, stopping immediately before the 2 marker.
    while abs(tr-r) > 1 and abs(tc-c) > 1:
        r += sr
        c += sc
        out[r][c] = 3
    if abs(tr-r) <= 1:
        while c + sc != tc:
            c += sc
            out[r][c] = 3
    else:
        while r + sr != tr:
            r += sr
            out[r][c] = 3
    return out
PY
